dedupe_keys.name: acs county to county migration flows

description: The County-to-County Migration Flows of the U.S. Census Bureau are origin-destination tables of people who moved between areas in the year before the survey, built from the American Community Survey and Puerto Rico Community Survey question on residence one year ago, crossed with current residence. For each pair of counties, and of county and minor civil division (MCD) units, the tables give movers with margins of error, sorted by current or previous residence, plus in-, out-, net and gross flows; flows between metropolitan statistical areas were added with the 2009-2013 dataset and flows from Puerto Rico municipios with 2008-2012. Special editions cross the flows by age, sex, race, Hispanic origin, relationship, household type and tenure. Coverage: the United States and Puerto Rico, from every ACS 5-year dataset from 2005-2009 to 2016-2020; the page notes a break in series after the 2016-2020 release. Format and access: XLSX table packages on the Census Bureau's www2 server, the Census Flows Mapper for county flows since 2006-2010, and the Census Data API for county, MCD and MSA flows since 2016; free and public domain. Caveats: flows are 5-year averages from a sample, small flows have very large margins of error, and no release has followed 2016-2020. Simulation uses: population redistribution and displacement scenarios, for example after disasters, long-term demand shifts between regions, and calibration of migration components in agent-based or land-use models. Related records: ACS commuting flows (the workplace counterpart from the same survey), Population and Housing Unit Estimates (which use migration components) and ACS tables.
